dct_creator_sm: Environics Institute for Survey Research (Environics Research Group, Toronto, ON).
dct_description_sm:
The dataset encompasses four Environics reports: Canadian public opinion about immigration and refugees, changing opinions about the United States, China, and Russia, COVID-19, public policy and government decision-making, and Canadian public opinion about racism and discrimination.

The Canadian public opinion about racism and discrimination report combines results from two public opinion surveys: Focus Canada Fall 2020 (the data file used for this analysis) and “A Better Canada: Values and Priorities after COVID-19.” The latter dataset is not included in this dataset and is not part of the Focus Canada dataset, so this distinction should be kept in mind when reviewing the report.

A question variable with no label was removed. The response options were (1 = Yes, 2 = No), but all responses were coded as “Yes,” providing no analytical variation.

As part of its Focus Canada public opinion research program (launched in 1976), the Environics Institute updated its research on key issues including: Canadian attitudes about immigration and refugees, Canadian attitudes about their country’s relations with its international partners, public priorities and on the ways in which governments make decisions, and Canadian public opinion about racism and discrimination.

This survey was conducted in partnership with the Faculty of Social Sciences’ IMPACT Project at the University of Ottawa and Century Initiative. This survey is based on telephone interviews conducted (via landline and cellphones) with 2,000 Canadians between September 8 and 23, 2020. A sample of this size drawn from the population produces results accurate to within plus or minus 2.2 percentage points in 19 out of 20 samples.
